identity.title: Turning Up the Heat: Min-p Sampling for Creative and Coherent LLM Outputs

problem.claim: The paper addresses how to sample next tokens from LLM vocabulary distributions while balancing generated-text quality and diversity, especially at high temperatures.

gap.claim: It identifies that popular top-p sampling often fails to maintain this balance at higher temperatures, producing incoherent or repetitive outputs.

contributions.claim: Proposes min-p sampling, a dynamic truncation method whose threshold scales with the probability of the top token to reflect model confidence.
Reports improved generated-text quality and diversity with min-p sampling, particularly at high temperatures, across GPQA, GSM8K, and AlpacaEval Creative Writing.
Reports adoption of min-p sampling in Hugging Face, VLLM, and other open-source LLM implementations.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors present confidence-scaled dynamic truncation as the defining feature of min-p sampling.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report benchmark results showing improved quality and diversity, especially at high temperatures, on GPQA, GSM8K, and AlpacaEval Creative Writing.
The authors report that human evaluators preferred min-p sampling for both text quality and diversity.
The authors report implementation adoption by Hugging Face, VLLM, and other open-source systems as evidence of practical utility and potential impact.

narrative_sequence.summary: LLMs sample each next token from a vocabulary probability distribution during decoding.
Top-p sampling is described as struggling to balance quality and diversity at high temperatures, with incoherent or repetitive outputs as consequences.
Min-p sampling dynamically adjusts truncation using the top token's probability as a confidence-scaled threshold.
Experiments and human evaluations are reported to favor min-p on quality and diversity, especially at high temperatures.
The abstract reports adoption in major open-source LLM implementations.

source_observation.claim: The abstract links a specific failure mode—high-temperature incoherence or repetition—to a method mechanism that adapts truncation to top-token confidence.

lessons.interpretation: A compact problem–mechanism pairing can make a sampling proposal's motivation and design rationale easy to assess.
lessons.application: When presenting a decoding method, explicitly connect the targeted generation failure to the parameter or rule that changes in response to it.
lessons.exception: This framing is unsuitable when the method's mechanism does not directly address the stated failure mode or when the abstract lacks evidence connecting them.

unknowns: The abstract gives no numerical effect sizes, baselines beyond top-p, evaluation protocols, sample sizes, or statistical uncertainty.
The reported adoption does not establish effectiveness, causal impact, or independently verified novelty.
